open_points.subject: Repair view (A15 rule 6) record selection
open_points.text: State 2 A15 rule 6: "the latest NodeExecutions ... of function nodes pinned to any contract version of that slot"; State 3: "for the repair view `surface` ... pages the NodeExecutions whose executed implementation is in that set"
open_points.question: Must the repair view include function-node NodeExecutions where `executed` is absent (`skipped_by_guard` / `upstream_failed`), or only records with an executed implementation id?
options: Include all function-node NodeExecutions for the slot's contract versions, including non-executed statuses
Include only NodeExecutions that name an executed implementation
open_points.default_guess: Include only NodeExecutions that name an executed implementation, as State 3 currently specifies.

open_points.subject: NodeExecution writer for restart recovery of in-flight effects
open_points.text: "NodeExecution M23 is written by `effects` for the record that concludes an operation element ... and by `runs` for every other record." + A11 rule 4: "when its attempt has no NodeExecution yet, the kernel writes it with status `outcome_unknown`"
open_points.question: Which module owns writing the `outcome_unknown` NodeExecution created during startup recovery for an in-flight EffectAttempt with no NodeExecution yet?
open_points.default_guess: `effects.recover_in_flight_attempts` writes it, because it is tied to EffectAttempt recovery and attempt-number coupling.

open_points.subject: Effect-class branching during run recovery
open_points.text: "No other module looks at effect classes." and `runs` owns "start-up recovery of runs left `running`" while A14 rule 5 requires branching: "a `read` element without one is sent again; an operation element of another class ..."
open_points.question: During `runs.recover_running_runs`, who performs the `read` vs non-`read` branch required by A14 rule 5?
options: `runs` reads effect class itself (directly or via bindings/flow data)
`runs` delegates each operation element reach to `effects`, and `effects` applies class-based behavior
open_points.default_guess: `runs` delegates to `effects` for each operation element, and `effects` applies the class-specific logic.
